Let’s dive into what you need to know! 🧵 #HMPV 1/8

nodes.author: India_Builds
nodes.text:
Who is at risk? While anyone can get HMPV, it’s more dangerous for:
Infants & young children 👶
The elderly 👵
Those with chronic conditions or weak immune systems
People in crowded places or healthcare settings #HMPV 
2/8

nodes.author: India_Builds
nodes.text:
How does it spread? HMPV spreads through:
Respiratory droplets 💨 (coughing, sneezing)
Touching contaminated surfaces 🖐️
Close contact with an infected person #HMPV 3/8

nodes.author: India_Builds
nodes.text:
Symptoms Mild cases:
Runny nose 🤧
Cough 🤒
Sore throat Severe cases:
Wheezing 😮‍💨
Bronchiolitis
Pneumonia
#HMPV 4/8

nodes.author: India_Builds
nodes.text:
How to prevent it?
Wash your hands frequently 🧼
Avoid close contact with sick individuals
Disinfect commonly touched surfaces
Cover your mouth when coughing or sneezing 🤲 #HMPV 5/8

nodes.author: India_Builds
nodes.text:
Is there a cure? No specific antiviral treatment for HMPV exists yet. Care focuses on symptom relief:
Rest 🛌
Hydration 💧
Fever reducers Severe cases may need hospitalization for oxygen therapy. #HMPV 6/8

nodes.author: India_Builds
nodes.text:
Why is it important? 

#HMPV may not be as well-known as RSV or the flu, but it can still cause serious complications, especially in vulnerable groups.

 Awareness is key! 🛡️ #HMPV 7/8

nodes.author: India_Builds
nodes.text:
Stay informed and stay safe! 💙

If you found this thread helpful, share it to spread awareness. 🙌 8/8
